summary: Orchestrator epoch bump creates 'invisible pin hole' during proactive prewarm causing silent fallback for pinned tenant
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary with proactive prewarm enabled, an orchestrator epoch bump coincided with an edge prewarm flush. Several tenants with explicit model version pins observed silent fallbacks to a degraded variant even though the control plane showed the pin intact. This manifested as higher error-tokens and degraded outputs for a small subset of requests without 5xxs on the edge.

Impact: Customer NebulaDocs (dedicated) reported degraded generation quality for ~0.6% of requests to a pinned route for ~18 minutes (03/10 02:14–02:32 UTC). No token billing anomalies observed but user-facing quality regressions occurred.

Observed behavior: Requests for pinned sessions were routed to a degraded fallback model variant without an explicit unpin event in control-plane snapshots. Routing logs show an epoch mismatch window where routing snapshots returned a cohort with a missing ephemeral pin (an "invisible pin hole") even though tenant metadata and audit logs show the pin present.

Why this is surprising: Pins are expected to be durable across orchestrator epoch bumps. The prewarm/flush path exposed a timing window where the edge routing mesh applied a newer epoch snapshot before the prewarm handshake completed, causing a transient drop in ephemeral routing state for affected tenant sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant route with explicit model pin and proactive_prewarm=true
2) Start a staggered canary promote (small percentage) with orchestrator epoch rotation enabled
3) Trigger an immediate prewarm flush on a subset of edge nodes (simulated via test hook) while epoch bump is in-flight
4) Send steady traffic with keepalive and streaming enabled; observe a fraction of requests routed to fallback variant despite pin existing in control plane snapshots
logs: 2026-03-10T02:14:12Z edge[proxy-12]/router INFO routing_snapshot_epoch=421 -> applied_epoch=422 tenant=nebula-42 route=/generate cohort_pin=absent cohort_cookie=xyz (controlplane_snapshot_epoch=422 pin_present=true)
2026-03-10T02:15:03Z orchestrator INFO epoch_bump initiated commit_id=abc123 prewarm_wave=3
trace_id=tr-00421 available in support trace store: https://traces.internal/redwood/tr-00421
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator bumps epoch and publishes snapshot; edge nodes race to apply snapshot while prewarm flush removes ephemeral cohort state leading to a short window where cohort lookup returns empty.
Hypothesis 2: Edge snapshot application logic prefers newest epoch but does not reconcile ephemeral cohort state until prewarm handshake completes, causing requests to fall back to default variant.
Reproduced in staging by triggering epoch bump + forced prewarm flush; confirmed ~0.4% silent fallback occurrences on pinned routes matching production pattern.
Telemetry: cohort_missing_rate spiked from 0.01% -> 0.6% at 02:14 UTC filtered by tenant tag=nebula-42 and route=/generate.
Correlated with orchestration PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/8199 which changed epoch publish ordering for faster rollout — rollback candidate considered.
comments: Aisha Khan (03/10 03:05 UTC): Customer reported quality regressions; attached example trace tr-00421 and customer sample outputs (redacted). Asked for escalation and timeline.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) (03/10 03:27 UTC): Initial triage — seeing epoch bump + prewarm overlap; reproducer in staging created. Hypothesis: ordering race between publish_snapshot() and prewarm_flush().
Elena Park (Routing) (03/10 05:12 UTC): Added defensive check to edge snapshot applier to avoid applying epoch N if prewarm handshake for N-1 hasn't reconciled ephemeral cohorts. Will test in canary.

Customer (NebulaDocs - PM, 03/10 06:00 UTC): Confirmed degraded outputs stopped after we disabled proactive_prewarm on the tenant route (per Support workaround). Asking for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

Marco Ruiz (03/11 10:24 UTC): Hotfix PR opened and merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/8213 — sequences epoch publish after prewarm flush completion. Deployed to us-east canary 03/11 12:00 UTC; no recurrence observed in canary window.
resolution: Hotfix deployed: orchestrator sequencing change ensures epoch publish waits for prewarm flush completions for affected waves. Immediate customer workaround: set proactive_prewarm=false on pinned routes until hotfix rollout. Rollout notes: hotfix rolled to us-east canary 03/11 12:00 UTC, staged to 50% nodes 03/11 13:00 UTC, full us-east 03/12 02:30 UTC. Monitoring shows cohort_missing_rate returned to baseline. Follow-up: additional telemetry to detect epoch-prewarm windows and a new agitator test in CI.
